<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/driver-turso`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**4** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/data-modeling/drivers.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport), syncSchemasBatch (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/virtual-objects.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via syncSchema (symbol, a method of class RemoteTransport))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **18** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `939d6c18dd6d1190b575d4cafb53707d9e630cc4` — the merge of head `f438ff8c00e75d42a955ac6a9c15578c0ac38e68` into base `f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 939d6c18dd6d1190b575d4cafb53707d9e630cc4 && git checkout 939d6c18dd6d1190b575d4cafb53707d9e630cc4
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729 f438ff8c00e75d42a955ac6a9c15578c0ac38e68 && git checkout -B drift-repro f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729 && git merge --no-ff f438ff8c00e75d42a955ac6a9c15578c0ac38e68

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f9dd03315030d5ef5edd491d5f0ea7211824b729` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `2687d387263b50ab07c20ed07fd1ca4015ef5e96`
Local-runs: none

PR #37425 (card #37345, route A of scope amendment 7181122299). Read: the card body and all six comments, the PR body and its four comments, the six-file net diff against `origin/main`, the 53 check-runs on this head (37 success, 16 skipped, 0 failure; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core`, `TypeScript Type Check` and every Lint family green; no name carries an older red run), and source on the head plus knex 3.3.0's `formatDefault`, read only.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies, each judged:

- **A1. Remote `ADD COLUMN` of a `storage.notNull` field with a literal `defaultValue` to a populated table: refused before, accepted now (NOT NULL kept, DEFAULT emitted, existing rows take it), through `syncSchema` and `syncSchemasBatch`.** Right. It is the card's defect and the local face's answer. `columnDeclarationSQL` keeps the #37281 rule unchanged (`notNull` survives a populated add only when `emitsDeclaredColumnDefault` holds) and now asks it through the local predicate itself. Pinned by `turso-remote-not-null.test.ts` case 5 on local and both remote doors (notnull 1, the row reads `'d'`, `tighten_not_null` empty, drift empty).
- **A2. Every remote `CREATE TABLE` and `ADD COLUMN` now carries the declared DEFAULT, nullable fields included.** Right as parity, with one consequence the PR does not name, see S1. Second visible effect: a nullable field with a literal default added to a populated remote table now back-fills the existing rows with the default, where they read NULL before. That is the local face's behaviour and is pinned (parity test, populated case); the changeset says it only for the `storage.notNull` case (N1).
- **A3. `NOW()` DEFAULT withheld on a populated `ADD COLUMN`; the row probe now also fires for an added `NOW()` column (`addsRowSensitiveColumn`).** Right, and it is what the amendment rules. Without the wider probe a sync adding only a nullable `NOW()` field would send the expression to a populated table and turn a working hosted sync into a refusal; ablation 3 in the dev report shows the pin. `declaresNowColumnDefault` asks the shared renderer, so a multi-value `NOW()` field triggers no probe and no withholding, as it gets no DEFAULT at all.
- **A4. Three new named exports on the `.` entry of the published `@objectstack/driver-sql`: `emitsDeclaredColumnDefault`, `sqliteDeclaredColumnDefaultSql`, `sqliteNowColumnDefaultSql`.** The exports themselves are right (one source, the remote copy `declaresEmittedColumnDefault` is deleted, no leftover reference). They ARE a public-surface widening; the declaration that says otherwise is wrong, see M1.
- **A5. `nowColumnDefault` SQLite branch now wraps `sqliteNowColumnDefaultSql(type)`.** Right: the three strings are byte-identical to the removed inline ones (date, the time CASE, the datetime default arm), so the local face's DDL is unchanged.

DEFAULT parity, remote against local, checked by reading `createColumn` → `applyDeclaredColumnDefault` → knex `formatDefault` against `sqliteDeclaredColumnDefaultSql`:

- Which fields get one: same predicate object (`emitsDeclaredColumnDefault`), same multi-value short-circuit (`isMultiValuedColumn`), same order. `formula` is skipped before either. Runtime tokens other than `NOW()` and object defaults: none on both. Identical.
- `NOW()`: same string per type from one function; the `NOW()` test precedes the boolean branch on both faces. Identical.
- Booleans: knex takes the `bool` branch only for `table.boolean`, which `createColumn` builds for `boolean` and `toggle` only; `KNEX_BOOLEAN_COLUMN_TYPES` is exactly that pair, and the renderer's expression `dv === 'false' ? 0 : dv ? 1 : 0` equals knex's. Identical.
- JSON: a multi-value or object default gets none on both. A JSON-typed scalar column with a scalar literal is a `text` builder on SQLite, so knex takes the catch-all; the renderer does too. Identical. Knex's `json` + object branch is unreachable because objects are refused by the predicate.
- Everything else: knex is `client._escapeBinding(value.toString())`, which for the SQLite client is the base `'…'` with `'` doubled; the renderer is `String(dv)` with `'` doubled. Identical for strings, numbers, booleans, the empty string.
- **Security (injection through a declared default string): no finding.** The only way out of a SQLite string literal is an unpaired `'`; every `'` is doubled; backslash is not an escape in SQLite; the value is always wrapped in quotes, numbers included, so no branch emits unquoted author text. The DDL goes as one statement through `client.execute` or as one element of `client.batch`, never through a splitter, so `;` or a newline inside the literal stays inside it. The `quoted: "it's"` row pins the doubling on both faces. The escaping is the same function the local face has shipped, so this adds no new class.
- NOT NULL interplay (`turso-remote-not-null.test.ts`): cases 1 to 4 are untouched and green; case 5 literal is one outcome on three doors; the `NOW()` half is recorded on both faces (local refuses nullable and `storage.notNull`; remote accepts nullable with `dflt_value` null and refuses `storage.notNull` with the earlier message). The record matches the code: for `storage.notNull` + `NOW()` on a populated table `notNull` stays true and the DEFAULT is withheld, hence the refusal.

Findings:

- S1 (should-fix) — The remote face now writes literal DEFAULTs it has no door to change. The shared differ reports `default_mismatch` (`drop_column_default` / `set_column_default`) when an author later removes or edits a literal `defaultValue`; `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS` answers both `needs-table-rebuild`, which the remote transport does not run. Before this PR a remote column carried no declared DEFAULT, so this drift could not arise there; after it, every hosted environment whose author changes a literal default keeps the stale DEFAULT (inserts omitting the field store it) with a finding it cannot apply. This follows from the card's own acceptance and the local face has the same report, so it does not block; but neither the PR body nor the changeset says it, and no card carries it. Owed: one sentence in the changeset, and a follow-up card for the remote DEFAULT rebuild limit (or a pointer to an existing one).
- S2 (should-fix) — The literal renderer is a hand mirror of knex whose stated guard is `turso-remote-default-parity.test.ts`, and that guard does not cover every branch the renderer has: `toggle`, a boolean field with the string default `'false'` (the branch the docblock names), the empty string, and a JSON-typed scalar column with a scalar literal are unpinned. Read against knex 3.3.0 they match today; a knex upgrade or a third `table.boolean` type in `createColumn` would fork the faces on those rows without a red test. Add the four rows to `DEFAULTED`.
- N1 (nit) — The changeset's second bullet does not say that a nullable field with a literal default, added to a populated remote table, now gives existing rows the default (NULL before). True and pinned; say it.
- N2 (nit) — The row probe and the `ADD COLUMN` are separate round trips, so a row arriving between them on a table probed empty makes a `NOW()` add fail with the non-constant-default refusal. Same window #37281 already has for NOT NULL, and the outcome is the local face's; record only.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/driver-turso` and `@objectstack/driver-sql` is right. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: the level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No key, accepted value or metadata type is added or refused, and `defaultValue` keeps its published meaning; the hosted face is brought to the behaviour the local face already has. The line is identical in the PR body and the changeset body.
- M1 (must-fix) — `Clause-②: no` is wrong; the line must read `Clause-②: yes (widening)` in the PR body and in the changeset body. The clause is not limited to `packages/spec`: its question is 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」 (`scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `execution-duties.md`), and 公开面 is defined as what a package's built entry declarations reach, with the `exports` map as the measure (`contract-review.md`). `@objectstack/driver-sql` is a published package (`publishConfig.access: public`) whose only entry is `.` → `dist/index`, and this diff adds three named exports to it, which the changeset itself announces as "New `@objectstack/driver-sql` exports". The api-surface and authorable-surface baselines cover `packages/spec` only, which is why no gate caught it; they are not the clause's boundary. Same-package precedent on main: changeset `35872` (three new `driver-sql` exports for the same remote-face sharing reason, `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch`) and the `driver-sql` CHANGELOG entry "`Clause-②: yes (widening: @objectstack/driver-sql exports PendingSchemaWorkKind from its index …)`". What the wrong value costs: the release notes file the entry under 其他修复 where a `yes` widening goes under 新增能力, and the contract-review face that a `yes` line owes is not owed on paper. The level does not move with the fix: `yes (widening)` beside `Metadata-protocol: none` stays `patch`, as in `35872`. Correcting the changeset moves the head, so this record does not carry over.
- Note on the other half of the line: the remote face accepting a declaration it refused (A1) is a pull-back to the declared contract and would by itself be `no`; the exports alone decide `yes`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flag, final-head comment 7182361715 ("the three new exports are a widening of that package's public surface; the PR declares `Clause-②: no`"): answered, M1. The dev's reading is correct and the declaration is not.
- `open_questions`, report 7181087036 (how to route the `NOW()` half; options A, B, C): answered by scope amendment 7181122299, route A. Accepted on the merits: B copies a local SQLite defect onto every hosted environment and breaks a sync that works today; C leaves the card's headline defect open behind a second card. A is an ordering split, not a product choice.
- `open_questions`, report 7181970667: empty. Nothing to answer.
- `NOW()` default on a populated `ADD COLUMN` keeps today's answer: verified in code (`columnDeclarationSQL` withholds it) and recorded in case 5 on both faces. Carrier #37413 is valid: open, `pm:queue`, `priority:p2`, `area:data`; its acceptance names the local fix, zero drift after it, and then the remote face's same answer through both doors with the removal of case 5's remaining `NOW()` note. `Fixes #37345` closing the card with that half moved is consistent with the amendment written on the card.
- Deviations in report 7181970667: (1) assignee on the PR, (2) a new test file because no shared harness file exists, (3) the PR body ending. None touches the contract; no finding. They are the lane seat's to accept.
- Gates the dev left NOT MEASURED (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`): left to CI; every Lint, Type Check, Build and Test run on this head concluded success, none failed. I did not map each of the three to its job by name.
- Docs Drift Check (advisory, 7181981898): no listed page states that the remote face emits no DEFAULT; nothing to correct found by grep on the head.
- SQL push-down (Prime Directive 5), every face: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The one read the diff widens is `populatedTableProbe`, `SELECT 1 FROM "t" LIMIT 1`: bounded, answered in SQL, one extra statement in `syncSchema` and one shared read batch in `syncSchemasBatch`, sent only when an added column declares `storage.notNull` or a `NOW()` DEFAULT. The DEFAULT itself moves work INTO the database (existing rows are filled by the DDL, not by an application back-fill). No finding.
- Escalated to the seat: S1's follow-up card (the remote face cannot drop or restate a DEFAULT it now writes).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37345-turso-remote-default`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## 席位核对

Head-sha: `2687d387263b50ab07c20ed07fd1ca4015ef5e96`
**REWORK** — L1, seat repo:objectstack#5: contract record 7182460866 reads FAIL on one declaration error (M1). The code holds; M1 and the two should-fix findings are fixed in this PR before landing.

1. **Shape**: open draft against `main`, 6 files (+413/−76), `Fixes #37345`, `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch changeset on `@objectstack/driver-sql` and `@objectstack/driver-turso`. `l1-face` is CLEAN: 37 success, 16 expected skip, 0 failed.
2. **Premise**: route A (scope amendment 7181122299) holds. The record finds remote and local DEFAULT output identical by reading for every type and default kind, from one `driver-sql` source. It finds no injection path (every value quoted, `'` doubled, no statement splitter), and the NOT NULL case 5 matches the code. The `NOW()` carrier #37413 is valid. No SQL push-down finding.
3. **Owed in this PR**:
   - **M1.** The three new `@objectstack/driver-sql` index exports widen a published package's public surface (`publishConfig.access: public`, single `.` entry). The clause's test is 「本卡放宽接受集或扩大公开面吗」, not spec-only, and `.changeset/35872-shared-record-ids-sql-compile.md` is the same-shape precedent. The PR body and the changeset must read `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. The level stays `patch`, and `Metadata-protocol: none` stays.
   - **S1.** The remote face now writes literal DEFAULTs it cannot later change. An edited or removed literal `defaultValue` gives `default_mismatch`, which `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS` answers with `needs-table-rebuild`, and the remote transport does not run that. Say so in the changeset, and file a follow-up card under #37345 for remote default drift.
   - **S2.** Pin the renderer branches the parity test misses: `toggle`, a boolean with string default `'false'`, the empty string, and a JSON-typed scalar column with a scalar literal.
   The same reviewer reads the delta.
4. **Accepted deviations**: nit N1 (the changeset could say a nullable field with a literal default, added to a populated remote table, now back-fills existing rows); add it with S1 if cheap. Nit N2 (the probe-to-ADD race on `NOW()`, same window as #37281) is record only.
5. **Out of scope and where it went**: `NOW()` on a populated ADD COLUMN goes to #37413; remote default drift goes to the card S1 asks for.
6. **Landing terms**: ungoverned, default tier. A same-head PASS with M1, S1 and S2 closed and an **ACCEPT** are owed. The area lands it.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `f438ff8c00e75d42a955ac6a9c15578c0ac38e68`
Local-runs: none

Delta review of PR #37425 (card #37345) over record 7182460866, which FAILED head `2687d387` on M1. Read: `git diff 2687d387..f438ff8c` (one commit on top, the old head is its ancestor, no main merge; 2 files, +38 −7: the changeset and `turso-remote-default-parity.test.ts`), the PR body at this head, os-dev-report 7182686626, cards #37430 and #37434, and the check-runs on this head (39 success, 18 skipped, 0 failure; `Check Changeset`, `PR-body guards`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Test Core`, `TypeScript Type Check` and `Lint & Repo Gates` green, the two names that appear twice are green on both runs). No source file under `packages/**/src` other than the test moved, so ①'s parity, injection and NOT NULL judgments of the earlier record stand unchanged on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

- A1 to A5 of record 7182460866: unchanged code, judgments carried. The net diff against `origin/main` is still the same six files.
- S1: closed. The changeset now carries a "Known limit" bullet: an edited or removed literal `defaultValue` is reported (`set_column_default` / `drop_column_default`), both need a table rebuild the remote transport does not run, the old DEFAULT stays and the finding stays reported; it cites #37430. #37430 is open, `pm:queue`, `priority:p3`, `area:data`, and its acceptance names the remote answer for both ops, `REMOTE_DRIFT_OP_ANSWERS` and `driftApplyLimit` moving with it, and a test for edit and removal. Valid carrier. The PR body says the same.
- S2: closed. `DEFAULTED` gained `toggled` (toggle, true → `'1'`), `empty` (text, the empty string → `''`) and `cfg` (json, 3 → `'3'`); the reference case asserts the three literal `dflt_value`s and the renderer equality loop runs over all `NAMES`, so each new row is held to the renderer, to all three `CREATE TABLE` doors, to the empty and populated `ADD COLUMN` cases and to the zero-drift read on both faces. The string `'false'` branch has its own describe: renderer `'0'`, local `dflt_value` `'0'`, remote `'0'` through `syncSchemasBatch`, `syncSchema` and `initObjects`. All four branches named in S2 are now pinned; CI is green with them.
- N1: closed. The changeset bullet "A nullable field with a literal `defaultValue`, added to a remote table that already holds rows, now fills those rows with the default … before, they read NULL" is in, and in the PR body.
- N2 (nit) — unchanged, record only: the probe and the `ADD COLUMN` are separate round trips. Not owed here.
- The `'false'` deviation (the row sits outside the zero-drift set): accepted. Verified by reading `physicalLiteralMatches` in `schema-drift.ts` at this head: only a `boolean`-typed declaration compares by truth; a STRING declaration `'false'` falls to the text arm and is unequal to the physical `'0'`, so the differ reports `set_column_default` on either face. That is a differ question, older than this PR on the local face, and the parity claim itself (one `dflt_value` on both faces and from the renderer) is pinned in full. Keeping it out of the drift read is the honest shape; forcing it green in this PR would have meant changing the shared differ outside the card's surface.
- N3 (nit) — #37434 says the false drift is "not introduced by that PR". True for the local face; on the REMOTE face it becomes reachable with this PR (no DEFAULT was written there before), and there the entry is also one the remote apply door cannot act on (`needs-table-rebuild`, #37430). Reach is a boolean field declaring the STRING `'false'`, and the outcome equals the local face's report. One sentence on #37434 would make the card exact; nothing owed in the diff.
- Nothing new introduced by the rework: the delta holds no product code, the new test rows use the existing harness, and the new describe reads no drift, as its comment states.

### ② Semver level

- M1: closed. `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial in the changeset body and in the PR body; `Metadata-protocol: none` beside it in both, with the same reason text. The widening is the three `@objectstack/driver-sql` index exports, which the changeset's last bullet names.
- Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/driver-turso` and `@objectstack/driver-sql`, unchanged and right: the level follows `Metadata-protocol` alone and `none` takes `patch` (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3; precedent `.changeset/35872-shared-record-ids-sql-compile.md`). `Check Changeset` is green on this head with the `yes (widening)` line, both runs.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: still right; the delta changes nothing an author can write.
- No `(narrowing)` arm, no BREAKING banner owed, no ADR-0087 marker owed.

### ③ Boundary flags
